findings.title: appStore export now returns promises while most consumers still expect modules
findings.body: The default export was changed from a map of module namespaces to a map of `import()` promises. Every existing `appStore[name]` access now yields a Promise unless the caller awaits it. This PR updates only a small set of call sites, so other consumers will read `.lib`, `.metadata`, or `.credentials` from a Promise and get undefined, breaking calendar, video, and payment integrations at runtime (and likely failing typecheck where the old module type is expected). Either keep a synchronous metadata map or update every consumer and the exported type to the async contract.

findings.title: getCalendarCredentials now silently returns calendar promises
findings.body: Because `getCalendar` became async, `getCalendarCredentials` now stores a `Promise<Calendar | null>` in the `calendar` field while remaining a synchronous function. Only `getConnectedCalendars` was updated to await that field. Any other caller of this exported function that treats `calendar` as a Calendar will call methods on a Promise. Make the function async and await `getCalendar`, or explicitly change the return type to expose promises and migrate all callers.

findings.title: Async forEach in reschedule is not awaited and try/catch cannot catch its failures
findings.body: `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async ...)` starts async callbacks but does not await the returned promises. `Reschedule` can return before `getCalendar` and `deleteEvent` finish, and the surrounding try/catch is ineffective for rejections from those awaits, producing unhandled rejections and potentially leaving calendar events undeleted. Use `await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(async ...))` or a `for...of` loop.

findings.title: Async forEach in reschedule is not awaited and try/catch cannot catch its failures
findings.body: `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async ...)` starts async callbacks but does not await the returned promises. `Reschedule` can return before `getCalendar` and `deleteEvent` finish, and the surrounding try/catch is ineffective for rejections from those awaits, producing unhandled rejections and potentially leaving calendar events undeleted. Use `await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(async ...))` or a `for...of` loop.

findings.title: requestReschedule fires calendar deletion asynchronously without awaiting it
findings.body: `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async ...)` now awaits `getCalendar` inside an async callback that the mutation never awaits. The mutation can return before calendar/video cleanup starts or completes, and failures become unhandled rejections rather than being handled by the mutation. Collect the promises with `map` and `await Promise.all` so reschedule cleanup is reliable.

findings.title: Recurring cancellation may skip calendar deletes because async forEach is not awaited
findings.body: In the recurring-bookings branch, credentials are processed with `forEach(async ...)`. The callback awaits `getCalendar` and only then pushes deletion promises into `apiDeletes`, but the outer handler does not await the callbacks. It may reach `await Promise.all(...apiDeletes)` before those deletions are pushed, leaving recurring calendar events undeleted, and callback rejections become unhandled. Convert this to an awaited `for...of` loop or `Promise.all` over the credentials.

findings.title: Dynamic imports are initiated eagerly, so app loading is not actually lazy
findings.body: Each `import("./...")` call in the object literal is evaluated as soon as `packages/app-store/index.ts` is imported. That starts loading/evaluating every app chunk immediately, so this change does not defer app loading and can still pay the full startup cost. If the goal is lazy loading, store thunks such as `() => import("./app")` and call/await only the selected app.
